title: Saffron: workload-harvester batch recommender with continuous safety budget
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build 'Saffron', a continuous batch recommendation engine that harvests workload signatures, synthesizes compact heuristics, and applies batching/caching configs with a safety budget and automated rollback. This ticket implements the profiler, the scoring model for candidate configs, the safe-apply orchestration, and observability hooks for regression detection.

Motivation: Manual batching tuning is slow, error-prone, and doesn't adapt to workload drift. Saffron should reduce per-token cost by recommending conservative-to-aggressive parameter families, validate them via shadow metrics, and execute a staged apply with automated rollback when quality or latency SLOs degrade.

Scope:
- Lightweight continuous profiler (sampled traces + feature extraction) running as a non-blocking sidecar.
- Candidate config generator: quantized set of batch_size/microbatch/window/kv_cache policies and prefix caching rules.
- Heuristic scoring: cost delta, latency tail delta, quality risk estimate (using eval-set signatures), and uncertainty score.
- Safe-apply controller: shadow apply, canary ramp, automated rollback based on configured thresholds and time windows.
- Telemetry & alerts: per-config dashboards, diffed histograms, and automated RCA hints.

Out of scope: model quantization automation, cross-region routing policies (handled by other tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Profiler runs continuously on 10% of requests and stores compact signatures (<=2KB) in the workload store
Candidate generator produces at least three config families (conservative, balanced, aggressive) for each workload signature
Scoring model outputs a ranked list with cost_delta, expected_latency_shift, quality_risk, and uncertainty fields
Safe-apply flow can shadow-apply a config for 1 hour and produce diffed metrics without impacting live traffic
Automated rollback triggers when latency P95 increases by >20ms or quality-score degrades by >3% in canary window
Dashboard shows before/after token cost, latency histograms, and a changelog entry for each apply
E2E test simulates a burst workload and demonstrates rollback within 5 minutes of threshold breach
implementation_steps: Design schema for workload signature (input length distribution, prompt-rate, KV hit ratio, common prefixes)
Implement sampling profiler as a low-overhead proxy that emits signatures to staging workload-store
Prototype candidate config generator and run offline sweep across historical traces to build priors
Implement heuristic scoring pipeline (cost estimator + latency model + risk model) and unit tests
Build safe-apply controller with shadow-apply capability and canary policy DSL
Integrate telemetry: metrics, traces, and dashboards; instrument regression alert rules
Run 2-week shadow experiment, analyze false positive rollbacks, and tune thresholds
Prepare rollout playbook and runbook for on-call; handoff to SRE for production ramp

rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Shadow only (two weeks): collect metrics, validate heuristics, tune uncertainty scores
Phase 1 - Canary conservative family (1% traffic, 24h windows): monitor latency P95, token cost, and quality probes
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp (1% -> 5% -> 20% over 3 days) for balanced family when canary stable
Phase 3 - Opt-in aggressive family for pilot customers and internal teams; require manual approval
Rollback policy: immediate rollback on any threshold breach in canary window; automatic rollback on sustained regression during ramp
